Cookie Storage Persist Behavior

Cookie Storage Persist is a Persist behavior that writes committed FeatureCell state to browser cookies during the Persist stage. It provides lightweight, session-scoped persistence using document.cookie and is intended for small, durable values that must survive page reloads without external storage dependencies.

This behavior observes the finalized pipeline output after all upstream processing—including resolve, merge, operators, filters, and reducers—has completed. The received value represents the authoritative, reduced state and is serialized and stored as a feature-scoped cookie.

Cookie Storage Persist does not transform values, emit snapshots, or influence pipeline control flow. Its role is limited strictly to persistence and hydration of finalized state in a predictable, fail-safe manner.

Storage Constraints

Browser cookies are limited to approximately 4096 bytes. To ensure safe operation across browsers, this behavior enforces a hard payload limit of 4000 bytes. Writes that exceed this threshold are rejected and logged without throwing.

When the persisted state is undefined, the associated cookie is removed entirely. When a valid value is present, it is serialized using JSON.stringify, URL-encoded, and written as a session cookie scoped to the FeatureCell.

Execution Semantics

Cookie Storage Persist executes synchronously within the Persist stage. Cookie writes and removals occur inline and complete before the pipeline proceeds. All errors during serialization, encoding, or cookie access are caught and logged without interrupting pipeline execution.

Note

Cookie-based persistence is best suited for small identifiers, flags, or lightweight configuration values. It is not recommended for large data structures, high-frequency updates, or sensitive information. For larger or more durable persistence requirements, alternative persist behaviors should be used.

Diagrams
Configuration

Cookie Storage Persist does not accept runtime configuration options. Its behavior is fully defined and deterministic, enforcing safe cookie size limits, serialization rules, and fail-safe execution by default.

Configuration consists solely of attaching or removing the persist behavior from a FeatureCell. When present, the behavior automatically participates in the Persist stage and observes finalized pipeline output.

Cookie Storage Persist may be freely stacked with other persist behaviors. When multiple persist behaviors are configured, each is invoked in sequence with the same final state value.

Examples

Example 1: Use the Cookie Storage Persist Behavior in a FeatureCell

This example demonstrates a FeatureCell configured with the withCookieStoragePersistBehavior . When state updates are committed via mergeState, the finalized FeatureCell value is written to document.cookie during the Persist stage.

Cookie Storage Persist observes the fully reduced pipeline output and performs persistence as a side effect. It does not transform values, influence merge semantics, or participate in pipeline control flow.

Note

Persist behaviors operate after all upstream stages—including resolve, merge, operators, filters, and reducers—have completed. Multiple persist behaviors may be attached to a FeatureCell and will be executed sequentially. 

{{`// app.config.ts

export const appConfig: ApplicationConfig = {
  providers: [
    provideVault({ logLevel: 'off' }),

    provideFeatureCell(
      EmployeeService
      {
        key: 'employees',
        initialState: []
      },
      [
        // Attach cookie-based persistence
        withCookieStoragePersistBehavior
      ]
    )
  ]
};

// bank-employee.service.ts

import { Injectable } from '@angular/core';
import { FeatureCell, injectVault } from '@sdux-vault/angular';
import { Employee } from './employee.shape';

@FeatureCell`}}<Employee[]>{{`('employees')
@Injectable({ providedIn: 'root' })
export class EmployeeService {
  readonly vault = injectVault`}}<Employee[]>{{`(EmployeeService);

  constructor() {
    this.vault.initialize();
  }

  addEmployee(): void {
    // Final state is persisted to document.cookie
    this.vault.mergeState({
      value: [{ id: 1, name: 'Jane Doe' }]
    });
  }
}`}}
 
{{`export const employeeCell = FeatureCell`}}<Employee[]>{{`(
  {
    key: 'employees',
    initialState: [],
  },
  [
    // Attach cookie-based persistence
    withCookieStoragePersistBehavior
  ]
);

// Initialize the FeatureCell
employeeCell.initialize();

// Commit state and persist to document.cookie
employeeCell.mergeState({
  value: [{ id: 1, name: 'Jane Doe' }]
});`}}
